title: Fly over Deosai, the land of giants and bears
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: High in Gilgit-Baltistan, between Skardu and Astore, lies one of the highest plateaus in the world: Deosai.
Let's fly in from the west, at around four thousand metres above sea level.
Below us is Sheosar Lake, at the edge of the plains.
Locals tell of a giant who once lived here. Deosai is said to mean the land of the giant.
In the Balti language, it is called Ghab-i-Yarsa, the place of summer.
The plains became a national park in nineteen ninety-three, mainly to protect the Himalayan brown bear.
In nineteen ninety-three, only nineteen bears were counted here. A twenty twenty-two survey estimated about sixty-six.
Deosai has the largest brown bear population in Pakistan, but the animals still face poaching and habitat loss.
Tourism brings new pressure. Researchers have found plastic and food packaging in bear droppings.
In summer, Gujjar and Bakarwal herders bring their cattle up to the plateau to graze.
The twenty twenty-two survey also counted twelve campsites, sixty-six tents and nearly five thousand livestock inside the park.
